policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the clause agentively: "the doings of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him". "Be rendered unto him" is an English passive for a causative verb with an unexpressed subject, matching the hiphil qere יָשִׁיב ("he shall render/repay to him"). The ketiv ישוב is qal and intransitive, which the ASV would have carried as the recompense returning to him, not as something rendered unto him by another; the verse has no ASV note bearing on the unit.
